creator_contract.design_scope:
Design the Episode tree for the task_specification (rev 3, entrypoint) under the operator addendum (rev 4), decision_ledger (rev 5), execution_policy (rev 2), interface_contract (rev 2) and safety_policy (rev 2). Read all six before emitting any workflow. For overlapping items, precedence is addendum, then ledger, then execution_policy. Nothing loosens safety_policy rev 2, which records the operator's egress exception and the answer-key resolution. Blocked closures use only the addendum's trigger vocabulary. The operator has resolved every question, including stop-and-checkpoint for 'wait until Monday' and an unknown weekly budget with the 1500 ceiling kept; do not reopen any.

Rulings: expect three readable ASM collections and record any mismatch. Each is a separate stratum with its own benchmark, noise floor, holdout, leaderboard, winner and findings. Process them SERIALLY, largest first, and close each fully before starting the next. No multi-collection requests and no cross-collection averaging. Each benchmark is corpus-generated, at most 40 questions, mostly multi-paper synthesis plus a control class. 20 or more synthesis questions is full power, 10-19 is low-power, and fewer than 10 is bound_hit benchmark_shortfall. incomplete_synthesis is never correct. Hold out 25%. Run the baseline 2-3 times to set the noise floor. Pivot discovery never uses hybrid, rerank or a trial config. Graph evidence counts only if it resolves to the collection. Always set use_graph explicitly. The Episode's own model only generates questions and judges, under one frozen, hashed prompt. The tenant's cheap sweep model performs every orchestration step via /v1/query. Strike infeasible structures at reconnaissance, with evidence. Confirm each winner on the strongest model, on the tuning set only.

Levels: the root unit is one per-collection study. Root progress is coverage-weighted per the addendum, whose A and B denominators are fixed: rerank sub-axes count only if rerank is kept, graph non-attributability counts as a strike, and modifier structures are outside B. Root stagnation counts only verified result-bearing closures. The run ends through the root terminal update once all readable collections are closed, or at a bound. None may be omitted.

Per collection: 1500 tenant billable calls. Setup takes at most 300, setup plus search at most 1200, and close-out 300. Phase A runs one generation trial per applicable parameter axis, then stops at 0.9 or after 3 sub-threshold gains on distinct axes. Phase B scores each feasible standalone structure on the phase-A winner. A collection is converged only if both phases complete; otherwise it is bound_hit with untried items marked not-tested. The holdout is model-matched and never informs a choice.

Run-wide stops (tenant budget exhaustion, which resets Monday, or an error-rate abort): stop all tenant calls at once, without retrying or waiting. Write the addendum's checkpoint, close every unclosed collection as bound_hit, and go to root close-out. Resuming is a separate approved run.

Enforcement: one run-wide HTTP client applying execution_policy's exact allowlist and a shared file-locked limiter; it refuses retrieve/query bodies without use_graph. The token is opened only inside that client. Write only to the run directory and scratch. Run the self-test before the first tenant call and the token-leak scan at close-out. The deliverable must match the extended manifest, and the terminal update must reference the hashed root manifest.

Binding: freeze benchmarks before scoring; screen via /v1/retrieve before generation; change one axis per trial from a named prior; resolve every citation via /v1/chunks; record a cost vector for every trial.

Prohibited: any tenant mutation, ingest, collection lifecycle or graph extraction, admin routes, and the model benchmark endpoint. The token at /Users/me/.patric_token is never written, logged, echoed or returned.

Report bound_hit never as convergence, untested axes as not-tested, and sub-noise deltas as within-noise.

deliverable.description: Results are materialized as files in one run-scoped directory under /Users/me/Development/OpenChia. The directory holds every item in decision_ledger rev 5 d_deliverable_manifest, as extended by operator addendum d_manifest_extension: per-collection studies, run-level records, any checkpoint, and a root closure summary. A hashed root manifest lists every file, and the terminal update references it. A typed status alone would not be usable, because the value is the auditable per-collection, per-trial and per-question record.

contract.goal: Determine, by measured read-only experiment against the BV-BRC RAGstack asm-next tenant, which retrieval and generation parameter combination and which episodic question-answering structure produce the best answers within each ASM paper collection measured separately, with the benchmark weighted toward multi-paper synthesis, leaving behind a per-collection winning configuration and the per-question evidence justifying it.

progress.description: Host-normalized progress of the root task Episode, derived from its typed terminal update. It is coverage-weighted: the sum of per-collection scores c, divided by the number of readable ASM collections (expected 3). A collection WITH a verified result-bearing closure scores c = 0.5 + 0.25*A + 0.25*B. Such a closure is converged or bound_hit, with a frozen benchmark, a noise-floor record from at least 2 repeats, at least one scored generation trial with outcome rows, and a leaderboard naming a current best, all hash-verified. Every other collection scores c = 0. A is the fraction of applicable parameter axes with a scored generation trial, and B is the fraction of feasible standalone episode structures scored; both denominators are fixed exactly by the operator addendum. 1.0 means every collection was fully compared on both. Quality scores are never averaged across collections.

contract.result: A run-scoped directory under /Users/me/Development/OpenChia with, per readable ASM collection: the winning configuration as a runnable JSON profile (every parameter, episode structure, confirming model); a trial leaderboard (parameter vector, tuning synthesis completeness, document coverage, noise-floor verdict, cost vector); per-question outcome rows (answer, cited doc_ids and chunk_ids, verdict, failure class); the frozen benchmark with gold evidence sets and holdout split; the noise-floor record; baseline and winner holdout scores with the overfitting estimate; a findings note on axes that mattered beyond noise, did not, or were not tested. Run-level: API and inventory snapshots, size and graph table, cheap/strong model choice with reasoning, frozen judge prompt and hash, cost totals splitting tenant calls from Episode-side cost, and a cross-collection note comparing strata without averaging.
contract.unit: One per-collection study: take one readable ASM collection from reconnaissance to closure. Build and freeze its synthesis-weighted benchmark (at most 40 questions; low-power rules below 20 synthesis) and holdout split, and set its noise floor. Phase A screens retrieval axes on document coverage, gives every surviving parameter axis at least one generation trial, then continues until stagnation across distinct axes. Phase B scores each surviving episode structure on the phase-A winner. Then run tuning-set model confirmation and model-matched holdout scorings within the projected close-out budget. Close with one typed status and a reason, and write the findings note. The repeated sub-unit is one tuning-set configuration trial with use_graph set explicitly. Axes that moved a collection beyond its noise floor carry forward as ordering hints; a hint never skips an axis or changes required evidence.
